gloss: to make known; to make widely known

definitions.gloss: to make known; to inform; to make widely known
definitions.explanation: To cause something to become known to many people. A formal, somewhat literary verb often used in declarations, announcements, or when describing how a person or thing gained recognition.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{名前|なまえ}を{世|よ}に{知|し}らしめた。
examples.english: He made his name known to the world.

examples.japanese: この{事件|じけん}は{報道|ほうどう}の{重要性|じゅうようせい}を{社会|しゃかい}に{知|し}らしめた。
examples.english: This incident made society aware of the importance of journalism.

examples.japanese: オリンピックでの{活躍|かつやく}が{彼女|かのじょ}の{実力|じつりょく}を{世界|せかい}に{知|し}らしめることになった。
examples.english: Her performance at the Olympics ended up making her abilities known to the world.

notes:
An archaic-flavored causative form of {知|し}る (to know), originally derived from classical Japanese. Carries a formal, declarative tone — common in news articles, biographies, and rhetorical writing, but rare in casual speech.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive (takes を). Often takes a target with に: 〜を〜に{知|し}らしめる (to make A known to B).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {世|よ}に{知|し}らしめる: to make known to the world
- {社会|しゃかい}に{知|し}らしめる: to make known to society
- {名前|なまえ}を{知|し}らしめる: to make one's name known
- {実力|じつりょく}を{知|し}らしめる: to demonstrate one's true ability

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {知|し}らせる: to inform, to notify — everyday word, much more common
- {広|ひろ}める: to spread, to popularize — emphasizes the spreading rather than the awareness
- {周知|しゅうち}させる: to make widely known — formal/administrative

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {知|し}らしめていませんでした
